recentItems.title: 1997 Edinburgh Tattoo - Massed Bands of HM Royal Marines
recentItems.description: Of particular note is the drum display. Although experimentation within individual bands had taken place in the preceding years, the 1997 Edinburgh Military Tattoo introduced for the first time to a wider audience, a visual effect that would become synonymous with the Royal Marines drum static: the ripple. Although a similar effect had been used during Riverdance at the Mountbatten Festival of Music the previous year, its use in the complex static Aurora Borealis was ground-breaking and was nearly pulled from the programme at the last minute when rehearsals proved more difficult than anticipated. However, the decision was made to go ahead and, in many ways, this saw the beginning of a new era in this genre . The ripple, and at a similar time slow stick-work, were revolutionary in terms of the progression of a very traditional style of drumming but both very quickly became accepted and are now a staple ingredient in any drum static.

recentItems.description: Commemorating the 219th Anniversary of the Battle of Trafalgar in 1805, the Sea Cadet Corps, supported by the other Cadet Forces, parade in Central London. They are led by the Massed Bands of the Sea Cadets, made up of cadets and adult volunteers from all over the UK.

recentItems.title: Royal Marines School of Music and Sea Cadets in Concert - Feb 2019
recentItems.description:
The Sea Cadets National Band Course was relaunched in February 2019 with support from the Royal Marines School of Music. After working together throughout the week, the cadets combined with the School of Music Band for an end of course concert in Portsmouth.

If you're a Sea Cadet or Royal Marines Cadet who plays a musical instrument and wish to get involved with musical activities (even if you are the only musician in your Unit), take a look at The Massed bands of the Sea Cadets Facebook Page and send the page a message.
